theme: Late-autumn larder: a pork & porcini ragu and a jar of confit garlic oil to carry the week (2 adults — girls are with Jen Nov 1-14)

components.name: Pork & porcini ragu
components.ingredients: 1.5 lb pork shoulder (cubed), 1 oz dried porcini, 1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 rib celery, 4 garlic cloves, 1/2 cup red wine, 1 can (28 oz) whole peeled tomatoes, bay, olive oil, salt
components.method: Soak porcini in 1 cup hot water. Pat pork dry, season, brown hard in olive oil in batches; set aside. Soften a fine soffritto of onion/carrot/celery/garlic in the fat. Add chopped porcini, deglaze with wine, reduce. Return pork, add crushed tomatoes, strained porcini liquor and bay. Barely simmer covered ~75 min until pork shreds; break it up with a spoon, reduce loose if needed. Keeps 4 days / freezes well.

components.name: Confit garlic & rosemary oil
components.ingredients: 3 heads garlic (peeled), 1.5 cups good olive oil, 2 rosemary sprigs, 1 dried chile, pinch salt
components.method: Put peeled cloves, rosemary and chile in a small pot, cover with oil. Hold at a bare simmer (55-60°C — just a few lazy bubbles) ~40 min until cloves are golden and spreadably soft; don't let them fry. Cool fully, jar cloves under their oil. Fridge up to 2 weeks — both the mellow cloves and the perfumed oil become weeknight shortcuts.

dinners.name: Pappardelle al ragu
dinners.ingredients: pork & porcini ragu, pappardelle (or rigatoni), parmigiano, olive oil, parsley
steps: Boil pasta in well-salted water; reserve a mug of water.
Warm the ragu, loosen with a splash of pasta water.
Toss drained pasta into the ragu off heat with a knob of butter or glug of oil until glossy.
Plate, shower with parmigiano, parsley and a thread of olive oil.

dinners.name: Soft polenta with pork ragu & gremolata
dinners.ingredients: pork & porcini ragu, polenta, parmigiano, butter, lemon zest, parsley, garlic
steps: Simmer polenta in salted water, whisking, until creamy (~25 min); finish with butter and parmigiano.
Chop gremolata: parsley, lemon zest, a little raw garlic.
Spoon polenta into bowls, ladle ragu over, scatter gremolata and a little more parmigiano.

dinners.name: Olive-oil poached cod with confit garlic, cannellini & salsa verde
dinners.ingredients: 2 cod fillets, confit garlic + its oil, 1 can cannellini, salsa verde (parsley, capers, anchovy, lemon), lemon
steps: Warm a small amount of the confit oil with a few confit cloves; add drained cannellini to warm through, season.
Heat a shallow pot of olive oil to 55-60°C; slip in salted cod and poach 10-12 min until just opaque.
Blitz or chop a quick salsa verde.
Spoon beans into bowls, set cod on top, lift out with a slotted spatula, spoon salsa verde over and finish with lemon.

dinners.name: Brothy clams with confit garlic, white wine & grilled bread
dinners.ingredients: 2 lb littleneck clams, confit garlic + oil, 1/2 cup white wine, chile flakes, parsley, crusty bread
steps: Grill or toast thick bread, rub with a confit clove.
In a wide pot, warm confit oil, mashed confit cloves and chile flakes.
Add clams and wine, cover, steam 5-7 min until they open (discard any that don't).
Finish with parsley and a glug of raw olive oil; serve with the bread to mop the broth.

technique.name: Low-temperature olive-oil poaching
technique.tiedTo: Wednesday's cod — hold the oil at 55-60°C with the fish just submerged for 10-12 min. The gentle, even heat sets the proteins slowly so the flesh stays silky and never seizes or weeps the way it can in a hot pan; a probe thermometer makes it foolproof, and the oil can be strained and reused.

shopping.items: 1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery rib, 4 heads garlic, 2 rosemary sprigs, flat-leaf parsley, 2 lemons
2 cod fillets (~6 oz each), 2 lb littleneck clams

1 oz dried porcini, 1 can (28 oz) whole peeled tomatoes, 2 cans cannellini beans, pappardelle (or rigatoni), polenta, good olive oil (large bottle — you'll use plenty), red wine, dry white wine, capers, anchovies, dried chile / chile flakes, bay leaves, crusty bread

scaleNote: This week is 2 adults (girls with Jen Nov 1-14), so quantities above serve 2 with ragu to spare. For the full-house weeks (6: 2 adults + 4 girls under 10): double the ragu and run it over rigatoni or into a quick baked pasta with mozzarella the girls love; triple the polenta and keep gremolata on the side so kids can skip it; double the confit garlic batch. For fish night, poach extra cod and set aside a few plain, unsauced pieces for the girls, serving salsa verde only for the adults; add buttered bread and a simple green salad to stretch any night.
